mutants.expected_detection: Running the wrap-triggering vector header_len=50000, payload_len=15536, dest_capacity=200 must return -1 and leave dest byte-for-byte unchanged. This mutant casts the widened sum back down to unsigned short before the comparison, reintroducing the 16-bit wraparound: 50000+15536=65536 truncates to 0 (mod 65536), which is <=200 and incorrectly passes the capacity check, after which the copy loops (still correctly bounded by header_len/payload_len) write 65536 bytes into a 200-byte dest, causing a massive out-of-bounds write and violating SR1/SR2.

Allocate dest with a red-zone canary region immediately after dest_capacity bytes. Run the wrap-triggering vector (header_len=50000, payload_len=15536, dest_capacity=200) and boundary vectors; the capacity check now uses >= instead of >, so a combined length exactly equal to dest_capacity+... is still fine, but more importantly the off-by-one direction change combined with the copy loops bounded only by header_len/payload_len means for the case total == dest_capacity+0 the check itself is not the flaw here -- the actual observable defect is that swapping the copy loop bound from header_len/payload_len to using 'total' (the widened sum) instead lets the copy loop run past dest_capacity when total slightly exceeds capacity in edge cases due to the inclusive comparison change, causing canary bytes immediately after dest_capacity to be overwritten, which is detected by comparing canary bytes before and after the call.

Running the in-range vector header_len=100, payload_len=100, dest_capacity=65535 (true sum=200<=65535) should be accepted with return value 200 and correct copied bytes. With this mutant, the capacity is artificially reduced by 1 before comparison (total > dest_capacity - 1), causing valid boundary vectors where total == dest_capacity to be incorrectly rejected with -1, and off-by-one false rejections near the true boundary, violating SR3's requirement that no false rejections occur for combinations whose true sum is <= dest_capacity.

FR1 vector header_len=4, payload_len=10, dest_capacity=32 expects return value 14 and dest[0..13] equal to header bytes followed by payload bytes. With the payload copy loop's increment removed, pos never advances during the payload phase, so all payload bytes get written to dest[4] repeatedly instead of dest[4..13], making dest[4..13] not match the expected payload sequence. The return value is unaffected but the buffer-contents check for FR1 will fail.

Test vector FR2 (header_len=0, payload_len=0, dest_capacity=0) must return 0 and must not write to dest. With the negated condition, total (0) > dest_capacity (0) evaluates false is flipped to negated form causing the zero-length case to incorrectly take the rejection path (or the inverse defect of dereferencing dest when it should not), producing return value -1 instead of 0, which is detected by an exact-match check on the return value for this vector.

For any header_len/payload_len pair whose true sum exceeds dest_capacity, the mutant still executes the copy loops before returning -1, writing header_len+payload_len bytes into dest (up to capacity overrun) despite the function ultimately returning -1. Test harness pre-fills dest with a sentinel pattern and checks it is unchanged after a rejected call (FR3) as well as canary bytes beyond dest_capacity (SR2); both checks will observe dest mutated even though the return value is -1, revealing the defect.

FR4 test vector header_len=dest_capacity, payload_len=0 (header exactly fills the buffer): the mutant's off-by-one comparison rejects this exactly-fitting case, returning -1 instead of dest_capacity, and dest is left unwritten instead of containing the header bytes. Detected by comparing actual return value and dest contents against the expected header_len == dest_capacity, dest == header bytes ground truth.
